title: LTM Ltd - 540005 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was USD 1.235bn, up 1.1% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, with INR revenue of Rs 11,808 crores (+13.6% YoY). EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

segments.name: BFSI (Financial services)
segments.commentary: Grew 3.1% QoQ and 0.4% YoY in constant currency, back to YoY growth after two sequential growth quarters. A financial services client was added to the USD 100mn+ category.

segments.name: Tech and services
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY but fell 4% QoQ on seasonal renewal cycle of top tech account (fiscal starts July) and Saudi business (routed via JV, classified here).

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Grew 0.3% QoQ and 8.6% YoY; travel and hospitality hit by fuel price and energy crisis, with customers tightening budgets.

segments.name: Production (Manufacturing, Energy & Utility)
segments.commentary: Grew 3.7% QoQ and 7.4% YoY, with both Manufacturing and Energy & Utility contributing.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas +1.5% QoQ, Europe +1% QoQ, Rest of World -1.4% QoQ due to Middle East (Saudi) revenue impact from the war.

guidance_outlook: Growth trajectory expected to strengthen through FY27; H2 to be better than H1 (H1 FY27 YoY growth 5.4%).
Q3 and Q4 expected to be sequentially better than Q1; management aims for FY28 to be a stronger growth year.
Target to keep FY27 consolidated EBIT margin at similar levels to FY26 (includes Randstad Digital M&A); Q1 and Q2 margins 15.5% and 15.6%.
Management aims to bring FY27 growth as close as possible to FY26 growth, not committed.
Randstad Digital acquisition approvals expected in Q3; closure by end of Q3, followed by 3-4 months to realign acquired Australia and Europe markets.
Remaining gratuity funding to complete by October; OCF/PAT expected to normalise in Q3 but not return to prior levels.
Forex losses below EBIT likely to continue for the next couple of quarters under layered hedging.
capex_capacity: Opened a new Global Delivery and AI Competency Center in Kolkata and expanded BlueVerse Studio footprint to Hyderabad.
A new business unit is being set up to build and scale GCCs (global capability centres), with GCC details promised in coming days.
Committed to build new domain-specific SLMs every quarter; three new SLMs created this quarter and six AI patents granted.
Cash and investments of about Rs 15,300 crores; payout ratio raised to about 45% last year from around 40%.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure, faster-revenue deals; management says majority of wins were AI-led and TCV is no longer the right KPI for the AI pivot.
Management indicated order book is largely ACV-based but will hold off on ACV disclosure for at least one more quarter.
Top BFSI client consolidating from 50+ vendors to about five; LTM is one of the five. Productivity headwinds already absorbed; about 60% of productivity headwinds passed to customers.
Traditional large deals are being fought at price points management called unmanageable; AI rate cards priced higher than traditional rate cards.
AI projects run 6 months to 1 year, with downstream data modernization, remediation and rationalization work; AI gross margins said to be better than traditional services.
Management says about 60-70% of the portfolio has completed the big-client deflation cycle; the remaining 20-30% goes through renewal and consolidation cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seasonal Tech decline recurring every year, and what is the Saudi effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech decline reflects the annual renewal cycle of the top tech account (fiscal starting July) plus Saudi business routed through a JV with a tech company. Management expects Tech to return to normal growth from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will TCV become less relevant, and will LTM disclose ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI deals are shorter and faster to revenue, so TCV understates them. ACV disclosure is planned but deferred by about one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 lost about 0.6-0.7% of growth to Saudi, expects H2 better than H1, and aims for FY28 as the stronger year; FY27 growth near FY26 is an endeavour, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidation from 50+ vendors to five is a multi-year benefit to LTM, with productivity headwinds already passed through in Q3-Q4 of last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said payout rose to about 45% from about 40%; reinvestment via M&A and organic investment (BlueVerse, GCC, talent) is prioritised. M&A is open but must be white-space and fairly priced.

qa_highlights.question: Has the macro or pricing environment changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said macro is unchanged over the last two to three quarters; traditional large-deal pricing is weakening, while AI rate cards carry a premium.

risks_watch: Saudi/Middle East disruption: Rest of World revenue fell 1.4% QoQ; management says it is beyond LTM's control.
Cash conversion: OCF/PAT of 39% and FCF/PAT of 24%; watch whether gratuity funding and advances normalise in Q3.
TCV and order inflow visibility: deal mix shift to short-tenure AI deals makes TCV less comparable; ACV disclosure is pending.
Randstad Digital integration: approvals expected Q3, and Q4 margin headwind from amortisation (CFO said not significant).
Traditional deal price erosion and industry-wide deflation expected to persist for a couple of years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI momentum and H2 recovery, but cautious on near-term growth, with the Saudi/Middle East impact and tech seasonality acknowledged. Management was evasive on ACV disclosure and FY27 growth, calling FY26 parity an endeavour, not a commitment.
key_quotes: When we started in Q1, I made a promise that every quarter will be better than the previous quarter.
So I am really confident about the next two quarters and also with the new capabilities we will inherit in the Q4, we should be very well positioned for FY2028.
And that is what we are trying to follow.
we are still working towards maintaining our margin at similar levels to last year.

growth.why: Management says H2 FY27 will beat H1 (H1 YoY growth 5.4%) and Q3/Q4 will beat Q1, and aims for FY27 growth close to FY26 (an endeavour, not committed); backing is a USD 1.3bn AI-centric order inflow and pricing, but ACV disclosure is withheld and no specific capacity numbers were given beyond a Kolkata centre already opened.
